# testdata/golden

Signatures produced by the **official AutoFirma**, used as the reference for
the structural diff described in `docs/validation.md` layer 1.

Generated by `tools/golden-diff.sh` from the jar that
`tools/fetch-autofirma.sh` downloads, signing the inputs in `testdata/inputs/`
with the same `testdata/certs/signer-rsa.p12` that openfirma uses. Point the
script at a jar you already have with `AUTOFIRMA_JAR=/path/to/autofirma.jar`.

Nothing here is committed. The point of the corpus is that it can be
regenerated on any machine against the AutoFirma version of your choice, so a
checked in binary would go stale and hide regressions.

Files, for an input called `simple`:

```
simple.autofirma.csig          CAdES reference, AutoFirma's output
simple.openfirma.csig          ours
simple.autofirma.dump          normalized tree of the reference
simple.openfirma.dump          normalized tree of ours
simple.autofirma.pdf           PAdES reference
simple.openfirma.pdf           ours
simple.autofirma.pades.dump    normalized structure of the reference
simple.openfirma.pades.dump    normalized structure of ours
simple.diff / simple.pades.diff   written only when the two sides disagree
```

The PAdES dumps come from `tools/golden/pdf-normalize.py`, which runs both
sides through qpdf first. It is deliberately not openfirma's own PDF parser:
see `docs/validation.md` for why that matters.
